title: Spend Governance, Contract Lifecycle, and Revenue Recognition Principles
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference’s centralized approach to spend governance, the contract lifecycle, and the high-level revenue recognition (RevRec) principles that finance and legal teams must apply when negotiating and operationalizing customer and vendor agreements. It aligns procurement approvals, contract review steps, and RevRec triggers to support consistent forecasting, accurate billing, and clean month-end close.
body_continued:
Scope:

- Applies to all purchase commitments, customer contracts, and recurring revenue arrangements executed by Redwood Inference or its subsidiaries.
- Includes self-serve sales contracts processed through the hosted API portal, Dedicated reservations, and Private deployment licensing agreements.
- Does not replace legal-formal interpretations for complex arrangements; use this as the operational baseline and consult Legal/RevenueOps for exceptions.

Principles and Objectives:

1. Single source of truth: Contract metadata (effective dates, renewal cadence, billing terms, SOWs, and discount approvals) must be recorded in the Contract Registry before signature.
2. Clear approval thresholds: Financial and legal approvals scale with commitment size and contract type to limit downstream RevRec complexity.
3. Forecast-first RevRec: Recognize revenue only when performance obligations are satisfied and appropriate evidence (invoicing, delivery, or access) exists.
4. Fast, auditable procurement: Keep review SLAs short (3-7 business days) to enable sales velocity while preserving controls.

Approval Matrix (high-level):

- Less than $25k ARR / One-time purchase: requisition owner + cost center manager. No Legal review for standard terms.
- $25k - $250k ARR or multi-year <= 12 months: Procurement + Finance approval; Legal review required for non-standard terms or special data residency clauses.
- > $250k ARR or multi-year > 12 months: Procurement + Finance + Legal + VP/Director approval. Executive sponsor sign-off if impact crosses capital commitment thresholds.

Contract Lifecycle (operational checklist):

1. Intake and Registration
   - Owner creates a Contract Registry entry with: counterparty, estimated ARR or spend, contract type (sales/vendor), key dates (effective, termination, renewal), billing model (prepaid/recurring/in arrears), and associated SOWs.
   - Templates: use the standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Order Form templates available in /contracts/templates.
2. Commercial Negotiation
   - Track material changes in the Contract Registry notes.
   - Any concessions to standard pricing or SLA credits must include a rationale and a Finance impact note.
3. Legal Review
   - Legal assesses IP, indemnity, limitation of liability, data residency, and confidentiality.
   - Legal turnaround target: 5 business days for standard deals; escalate to Legal partner if >7 days.
4. Signatures and Storage
   - Prefer e-signature (DocuSign). Final signed PDF + executed SOW must be uploaded to the Contract Registry and to the secure Contracts SharePoint folder.
5. Post-signature Operations
   - RevenueOps sets up billing schedules; Procurement/Internal Ops records vendor obligations.
   - Finance maps revenue elements to RevRec categories (subscription revenue, professional services, one-time fees).

Procurement Procedures and Controls:

- Competitive Procurement: For purchases > $50k, obtain at least two vendor quotes unless sole-source justification is recorded.
- Purchase Orders (POs): All vendor engagements requiring upfront payment or multi-month commitments must have a PO before procurement executes.
- Delegation of Authority: Spending approvers validate budget availability in the FP&A system prior to approval.
- SLAs:
  - Procurement intake acknowledgement: 48 business hours.
  - Initial vendor evaluation: 5 business days.

Revenue Recognition (Practical Guidance):

- Accounting policy summary (aligned to ASC 606 principles):
  1) Identify the contract with a customer.
  2) Identify the performance obligations.
  3) Determine the transaction price.
  4) Allocate the transaction price to performance obligations.
  5) Recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation.

- Common patterns at Redwood: 
  - Hosted API usage (consumption): Recognize as services are delivered; invoicing is monthly in arrears. Usage meters are the objective measure of delivered performance.
  - Dedicated reservations (committed capacity): Recognize ratably over the commitment period unless there are explicitly separate deliverables (e.g., onboarding) which are recognized when delivered.
  - Private deployment / licensing + support: License fees allocated between the software license (may require upfront recognition considerations) and annual support (recognized ratably). Consult RevenueOps for allocations for large multi-element arrangements.
  - Implementation/professional services: Recognize on completion of the milestone or using percentage-of-completion where milestones are not discrete and measurement is reliable.

Journal triggers and deferred revenue handling:

- Cash received before performance (prepayments, annual pre-billed contracts): record as deferred revenue (liability) and amortize to revenue according to the recognized pattern.
- On cancellation with refund liability: recognize reversal of previously recognized revenue only for periods not yet delivered; account for restatement if material.
- Credits and refunds: route through the billing adjustment workflow and maintain support ticket link in the Contract Registry for audit trail.

Billing and Invoicing Policy:

- Billing cadence: default monthly in arrears for usage; quarterly or annual in advance allowed when contractually agreed.
- Invoice content minimums: invoice date, invoice number, PO number (if provided), contract ID, billing period, line-level description mapped to product codes, tax treatment, payment instructions, and contact for disputes.
- Dispute resolution: disputes must be logged in the Billing Dispute Tracker within 10 business days of invoice receipt; do not withhold payment unless dispute resolution terms permit.

Forecasting and Budget Integration:

- Input cadence: Sales bookings and quotes must be entered into the FP&A pipeline tool within 24 hours of signature. Procurement committed spend is captured weekly.
- Rolling forecast: maintain a 12-month rolling forecast updated monthly and a 5-quarter operating plan refreshed each quarter.
- Variance analysis process: monthly variance report comparing actual vs forecast for revenue and top-5 vendor spend categories; owners required to explain variances > 10%.

Operational Playbooks and Tools:

- Contract Registry (single source): fields required: contract_id, counterparty, owner, contract_type, start_date, end_date, auto_renew_flag, billing_model, estimated_ARR, legal_review_status, signature_date, storage_location, revrec_category.
- Templates and checklists: available at /confluence/finance-and-legal/templates, including a Vendor Security Checklist and Billing Template.
- Automation: RevenueOps owns scripts that pull contract metadata into accounting system staging tables; do not modify these scripts without coordination.

Escalation and Exceptions:

- Exceptions to the approval matrix require documented business justification and sign-off by the Finance Director and the General Counsel.
- If Legal review extends beyond the SLA, notify Sales/Procurement and schedule a triage meeting within 48 hours.

Ownership and Contact List:

- Finance Director (RevenueOps): Michael Chen — revenue policy, RevRec allocation, and forecast integrity.
- Head of Procurement: Sofia Ramirez — procurement process, vendor sourcing, PO controls.
- Senior Counsel, Commercial: Daniel O'Neill — contract language, risk exceptions, special terms.

Implementation timeline and next steps:

1. Immediate (30 days): Mandate Contract Registry entries for all new contracts; retrain Procurement and Sales on template usage.
2. Near term (60-90 days): Deploy updated billing template to invoicing system and implement automated PO-blocking for purchases without approved POs.
3. Quarter (Q2): Run a table-top audit of 25 recently closed contracts to validate RevRec classification and PO compliance.
